title: MySQL Introduction
summary: Learn what MySQL does. Think of a database as tidy sheets of information, then try three tiny SQL questions.
introduction: Imagine a school list with a name and a score on each row. A database keeps information in a tidy way. MySQL is a program that looks after databases. We use a language called SQL to ask it questions. Begin with questions that do not change any stored data.
learningObjectives: Explain what MySQL and SQL do
Ask MySQL to show text and do maths
Tell a database table from a spreadsheet picture

rows: Data arranged in rows and named columns.
The language used here to ask MySQL for data.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/mysql/installing-connecting) to use MySQL on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
SELECT asks for a result. Text goes inside single quote marks. AS gives the result column a name.
MySQL can work out small sums. This does not need a table. The result has one column called pencils and one row containing 5.
UPPER returns text in capital letters. It does not change any stored row in this example.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: The site SQL playground uses SQLite. These lessons explain MySQL. Many simple commands work in both, but some rules and commands differ.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change the name in the greeting. Then ask MySQL to add 6 and 4.
